National Assembly
Upper House
Nineteenth Session
Complete Minutes of Proceedings
Friday, Falgun 9, 2082
Meeting Number
The meeting of the National Assembly commenced today at 12:19 PM under the chairmanship of the Right Honourable Chairperson, Mr. Narayan Prasad Dahal.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Members – (12:19 PM)
Proceedings begin. Honourable members have submitted their names to speak during Zero Hour. I have allocated 1 minute to each Honourable Member to speak during Zero Hour. First, Honourable Member Ganga Kumari Belbase.
Honourable Mr. Ganga Kumari Belbase (Nepal Communist Party, Maoist Centre): – (12:19 PM)
Sir, in Bhairavi Rural Municipality Ward No. 1, Jaldire, Dailekh District, Karnali Province, exploration, research, and measurement have revealed the presence of 80 billion 700 million cubic meters of natural gas. Methane gas is considered a cleaner fuel than petrol and diesel. China's state-owned geological survey conducted the exploration. The exploration in Jaldire is in its 44th phase. With the commencement of commercial production, it will generate significant revenue, which will reduce Nepal's economic burden. It can make a significant contribution to the national economy and save foreign currency. I wish to state that the government should prioritize its excavation to fulfill this need and national requirement. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Gopal Bhattarai.
(12:20 PM)
Honourable Mr. Gopal Bhattarai (Nepal Communist Party, UML): – Honourable Chairperson, it is heard that out of 59 contract employees at the Social Welfare Council under the Ministry of Women, 16 employees have been dismissed. If they were not to be kept on contract, then all should have been dismissed. Otherwise, we have received information that only 16 individuals have been dismissed based on various allegations and accusations. In such a situation, if the government acts this way in the final stages of the election, the Election Commission may raise concerns about whether discipline is being maintained or not. (... Time expired.)
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Gopi Bahadur Sarki Achhami.
(12:21 PM)
Honourable Mr. Gopi Bahadur Sarki Achhami (Nepal Communist Party, Maoist Centre): – (.. Sound not audible ..)
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Maya Prasad Sharma.
(12:22 PM)
Honourable Mr. Maya Prasad Sharma (Nepal Communist Party, Maoist Centre): – (.. Sound not audible ..)
(12:23 PM)
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Sharda Devi Bhatta.
(12:23 PM)
Honourable Ms. Sharda Devi Bhatta (Nepal Communist Party, UML): – Honourable Chairperson, the current pressing issue is that only 20 days remain for the election in the country. Therefore, through you, Mr. Chairperson, I want to tell the Government of Nepal that the election should be conducted in a peaceful, fair, impartial, and non-violent manner, adopting a code of conduct with restraint. I wish the current government success. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Sumitra BC.
(12:24 PM)
Honourable Ms. Sumitra BC (Nepal Communist Party, UML): – Honourable Chairperson, news of increasing murder and violence in various parts of the country is coming in. On Wednesday, Magh 28, 2082, in Janakpur, 23-year-old Alita Khatun was murdered by strangulation with a rope. Similarly, in Dailekh district, on Dullu Campus Road, Prakash Khatri, a 10th-grade student, was murdered by the use of a sharp weapon by a friend. I offer my heartfelt condolences to the deceased and demand that the government thoroughly investigate such incidents, take stringent action against the culprits, and provide justice to the victims. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: The order in which Honourable Members spoke during Zero Hour concludes here. As per the constitutional provision, one-third of the Honourable Members, having completed their six-year term, will be retiring from Falgun 20, 2082. Honourable Members who wish to present their experiences will be given time to do so. For this, I have allocated 12 minutes to each Honourable Member. First, Honourable Member Gopi Bahadur Sarki Achhami.
(12:24 PM)
Honourable Mr. Gopi Bahadur Sarki Achhami (Nepal Communist Party, Maoist Centre): – Honourable Chairperson, first, I want to remember all the warriors who sacrificed their lives in this transformative movement, especially those who sacrificed their lives in the ten-year People's War for the country's significant political transformation. And today, being the 39th People's War Day, I extend my heartfelt greetings on behalf of myself and my party to all the respected mothers, fathers, brothers, and sisters who have played their role in all the changes. I was first represented in the National Assembly from Koshi Province in 2076 from the then-Communist Party of Nepal. Of course, after that, many incidents occurred in the country, and changes took place. Especially with the division of the Communist Party, and after the party from which I was represented in the National Assembly six years ago split, we are now bidding farewell again as members of the Nepal Communist Party, Maoist Centre, and currently as members of the Nepali Communist Party, representing in the National Assembly. I feel that during these six years, we faced many challenges, many complexities, and difficult national political situations. Specifically, during these six years of political tenure as a member of this National Assembly, the parliament was dissolved three times. The first dissolution of parliament was reinstated through the courts with the strength of street protests by all transformative political forces. The second dissolution of parliament was again reinstated through the courts, especially with the conscious initiative of civil society, the intellectual class, and political parties. The third dissolution of parliament occurred due to the dissatisfaction expressed in society in the form of the 'Jana Andolan' (People's Movement), and due to that dissatisfaction, this parliament was dissolved. We are going to the mid-term elections on the 29th to resolve this pragmatically. The country is moving towards a situation where the parliament will be reinstated in a new way, or the parliament will move forward, in order to institutionalize democracy, ensure the implementation of the constitution, and institutionalize all the achievements of the transformative movement to advance the country, in line with the practice of democracy, we will be approved through elections. In this context, the government has taken a significant responsibility. The responsibility to protect democracy, protect the constitution, protect the republic, and conduct the historic election within that responsibility is immense and important. There is fear in society, and some people are saying that elections will not happen. Due to the uncertainty among voters and the general public, this responsibility is extremely profound and important, and I request that the government fulfill it accordingly. The constitution was formed by integrating the spirit of the ten-year People's War, the nineteen-day People's Movement, and the Madhesh Movement. It is a document of consensus that, from the perspective of nationality, strengthens internal national unity, ensures inclusivity, and establishes a federal democratic republic, which is a significant mandate of the constitution, achieved through the understanding and initiative of political parties, leading the country to its current state. However, I feel that the transformation of society or revolution cannot be completed by a single phase of revolution and that it continuously demands revolution or continuous change. We have constitutionally established the republic, federalism, inclusivity, and ensured the rights of the oppressed, but due to the lack of laws to manage and implement fundamental rights, or due to the weakening of revolutionary forces, and because the change in the country that occurred through the process of revolution is moving forward in an evolutionary manner, there have been problems in delivery. Trust in federalism, political parties, the government, and the state has gradually eroded, leading to a state of rebellion, which was expressed in the form of the 'Jana Andolan'. When we failed to institutionalize the revolution, when we did not show promptness in the practical implementation of the revolution's achievements, and when the government kept changing in a musical chair-like fashion, I call it the failure of coalition governance. We cannot end coalition governance until we move towards a permanent system, ruling for 54 years, forming governments, or advancing the state in that direction. Otherwise, such complexities will continue to arise in the country, and I anticipate even more complex situations. I am currently going among the general public and voters during the election process. I am also going among the new youth, understanding the psychology of the old comrades, the psychology of the voters, and the needs and demands of the new comrades. Looking at this situation, I still feel that these elections will not solve the political problems. However, my request is that the political problems must be resolved. Now, the situation that has arisen in the country, we have made the constitution, the state has changed, centralism has been broken, and the movement has brought the country to a point where the people, especially the oppressed Madhesis, Muslims, Karnalis, Janajatis, Dalits, and women, can become owners of this state. However, some complexities in its practical implementation are the complexities of lawmaking, the complexities of rule-making, and we have not been able to resolve these complexities. The government that comes after the new elections needs to be prompt in addressing them. Secondly, our National Assembly has operated through understanding and cooperation. I came here from a certain situation, environment, political background, family background, and social background. I sometimes say that I came here at a young age; this is a gathering of elders, a council of experienced, seasoned, and senior individuals. When I came, I was around 45 years old. I feel I came a bit early, but I came to the university, and here I had the opportunity to cooperate with many politically mature leaders. I had the opportunity to cooperate with senior leaders, chief whips, and other Honourable Members from all political parties. I feel I have relatively fulfilled my role in initiating lawmaking to raise public issues from my position and in showing interest, concern, and pressure regarding the government's actions. In terms of cooperation, the former chairpersons of the National Assembly and the current chairperson have provided guardianship. As party leaders, my leaders like Dinanath Sharma, then Narayan Kaji Shrestha, and others...

The honorable chairperson guided me, and primarily, our party leader, the honorable Comrade Prachanda, as he entrusted me with the responsibility of Chief Whip. I also got the opportunity to fulfill my role in the management. As the chairman of my party, I would like to extend my heartfelt thanks to the honorable Comrade Prachanda. Similarly, the General Secretary, perhaps two General Secretaries have changed, the Secretary of the National Assembly has also changed. I have collaborated with approximately three Secretaries. Likewise, I would like to express my sincere gratitude and thanks to the committee chairpersons, staff colleagues, and all colleagues from the secretariat who provided cooperation and an opportunity to work in a cordial environment. The country is now moving forward with elections approaching. What will be the situation after the elections? I would like to conclude my remarks by expressing my heartfelt thanks and gratitude to the honorable chairperson and the secretariat for this opportunity, with my commitment to utilize my remaining experience in social service, national service, and social work. Thank you. Namaste.

Honorable Chairperson: The process of honorable members presenting their experiences is underway.

(12:38 PM)

Time for speaking is allocated on a party basis. Time for regional concerns.

Honorable members have submitted their names. Now, I will provide time for honorable members to speak. First, honorable member Urmila Aryal for 12 minutes. Following this, honorable member Durga Gurung.

Honorable Shri Urmila Aryal (Nepal Communist Party, Maoist Centre):

(12:39 PM)

Honorable Chairperson, before I present my views, I would like to pay tribute to Dr. Meena Acharya, who passed away yesterday. She established a system for valuing women's contributions and recognizing their work. For the work she did, she played a significant role in initiating the process of estimating how much women could earn and in collecting data for it. Therefore, on behalf of all the women of Nepal, I would like to express my heartfelt tribute and respect to her.

Now, utilizing the time for provincial special issues, as I represent Madhesh Province, I wish to begin by speaking about it. Madhesh Province is a granary and a fertile region for agricultural production. Out of 442,580 hectares of land, 502,224 hectares are cultivated. The main crops are paddy and wheat; Madhesh Province is indeed a granary for the rest of the country. In terms of economically active population, it is 57.7 percent. As I mentioned earlier, the main crops are paddy, followed by wheat, sugarcane is also produced, and vegetables are also grown well. There is also a good arrangement for animal husbandry, poultry, fruits, milk, and fish. Sugarcane production in the country is 66.5 percent from Madhesh Province. Oilseed production is 22.1 percent. It is rich in fruits like mangoes, litchis, and bananas. Ten lakh liters of milk are produced here. It is also a place with good fish production. Therefore, among all the provinces of Nepal, I believe Madhesh Province is a food-rich province in this regard. Artistically, Mithila art is very famous. There are also plenty of industries based on the textile industry, furniture manufacturing, domestic production, cement, pipe factories, and medicine production. In terms of cultural heritage, there is Janaki Mandir, Mithila art, Gothimai in Bara, Kadalani Mai in Sarlahi, Gahwamai in Birgunj, and Simraungadh is a historical fort. However, regarding these cultural heritages, the lands are being encroached upon, and their records are lost. When I visited Simraungadh, I saw only one pond of 40-42 bighas at that time. Around it, there were large rose gardens with extensive banana cultivation and personal vegetable gardens. I visited when I was studying BA. However, when I went recently, all the land around the palace has been encroached upon. That pond is also gone; it has been greatly misappropriated. I believe the government should investigate it again, conserve those heritages, and develop them as a tourist destination. As I am also a representative of the government, I wish to draw your attention to this matter.

There are many other problems here. In terms of human resources, there are problems of unemployment, poverty, floods, and inundation, and gender inequality. Regarding gender inequality, the participation of women as village chairpersons, vice-chairpersons, provincial assembly members, or ward chairpersons is declining. The number of women ward chairpersons in the entire country is very low, and it is even weaker in Madhesh Province. Furthermore, the educational level of the daughters of Madhesh Province is not very high, making them somewhat backward. It used to be that they did not come here much. That is true. Now, with our open border, we bring educated daughters from India as brides, and they get more opportunities when they become village chairpersons, vice-chairpersons, provincial assembly members, etc. Therefore, Madhesh Province appears to be lagging behind in educating its own daughters. The government needs to conduct door-to-door campaigns for education. We, as representatives of the province, also need to take the responsibility of conducting door-to-door campaigns to encourage daughters to pursue higher education. I felt this when I was sending proposals from various organizations and going to ask for them. That is why I am raising this issue today. I have also given this suggestion in a few places. Now, there is an increase in women's empowerment, cooperative strengthening, political participation, self-reliance, and entrepreneurship. And primarily, there are minority communities there, including Muslims, and those from lower castes like Dom, Dusadh, Chamar. These communities face extreme oppression. They live in small huts in marginalized areas without toilets in their homes. We often hear news of daughters being raped while going outside to use the toilet, some losing their lives, and falling victim to gang rape. You must have also read about such incidents in newspapers. Therefore, for Madhesh Province, specifically for the ethnic backwardness, the oppression faced by the Dalit community, and the practice of not recognizing them as human beings, there is a need to bring special budgets and programs for Madhesh Province to increase their prosperity and human development index. I also wish to draw the attention of the provincial government to this matter.

Besides this, Mithila art is extremely famous worldwide. I felt during my recent visit that its marketing is currently lacking. We have not been able to commercialize it properly. Therefore, to promote it in other countries, we need to bring special programs. The beautiful artworks they create. When I visited before and now, the number has decreased significantly. If we can conserve it and export it, and if government offices at least buy and display Mithila art, and if the government can implement a policy to promote Mithila art in all government offices, then that art can be revived. I would like to make this suggestion and draw your attention to it. The Madhesh Province has its own unique identity. Every year on the first of Baisakh, the Sahales flower blooms. It blooms in the form of a garland, and it lasts only for a day, on the first of Baisakh, based on the love story between King Sahales and a woman who worked as a gardener. This uniqueness can attract many tourists if promoted, especially in our neighboring countries. I urge the government to allocate a budget for the development of that region.

Furthermore, there are marginalized communities, including Muslims, Harijans, oppressed communities, minorities, etc. Special programs need to be implemented for them. Otherwise, they will remain backward and neglected. Everything is evaluated based on the majority, and more focus is given to communities with larger populations. Minority communities tend to remain marginalized and in the background. Therefore, this needs to be addressed with attention. Similarly, in the preservation of languages, we have Maithili, Bhojpuri, Bajika, and other local languages. We need to focus on preserving these languages. Whether they are minorities or marginalized communities, we need to conduct a proper assessment of their languages, prepare studies and data, and determine how to promote them and how to preserve them. These diverse languages are our heritage, and we need to pay attention to them.

It is ahead in agriculture and animal husbandry, but from the government's side, we need to promote it further and provide more incentives. Regarding agricultural research, I want to mention the Agricultural Research Council. There are six regional agricultural research stations, but there is a lot of corruption, and they are not managed properly. Farmers should also be included in the ownership of these boards. Then, they can also participate in the decisions made there and properly protect their rights. Therefore, boards need to be formed for every Agricultural Research Council, and key farmers from fisheries, horticulture, fruit production, paddy cultivation, and wheat cultivation should be included in these boards. This will help uplift the farmers, and agricultural research work needs to be managed better. Similarly, the hill tribes are in a somewhat minority status. The hill tribes are not even counted, so there is a need for better arrangements for the conservation of these hill tribes who originated from the hills. Similarly, Muslim communities, Yadavs, and Hindus are the majority. In this way, the Tharu population is in the Terai region, below the Chure-Bhawar region... (Time expired).

Honorable Chairperson:- Honorable member Durga Gurung. Time 12 minutes.
(12:51 PM)
(12:52 PM) (Point of Order): Honorable Mr. Padam Bahadur Pariyar (Nepali Congress):- Honorable Chairperson Sir, I wish to raise a point of order. As per Rule 21 (d) 1 of the Rules of Procedure of the National Assembly, I wish to raise a point of order. Just now, a statement was presented in the assembly that insults more than 6 million Dalit communities of Nepal, and that the Constitution of Nepal has not made any provision to differentiate between the more than 30 million population of Nepal as upper caste, lower caste, mean caste, high caste. I also wish to condemn this. There is no such provision in Nepal. There is no such provision in any law, and it is not permissible to express views that insult the Dalit community in this manner in the assembly. Therefore, I request that this be removed from the record and rejected. Thank you.
Honorable Chairperson: Regarding the subject on which the honorable member has raised a point of order,
(12:53 PM)
I direct the Secretariat to study if there is anything outside the rules. Honorable member Durga Gurung, time 12 minutes. After this, Honorable member Sumitra BC.
Honorable Mr. Durga Gurung (Nepali Congress):- Honorable Chairperson,
(12:43 PM)
I wish to present some of my views. I have stood here today with the intention of sharing some of my thoughts on the upcoming House of Representatives member election, which is scheduled to take place in 20 days. Honorable Chairperson, the country is gradually becoming election-focused. On the upcoming Falgun 21st, elections for the House of Representatives members under the Federal Parliament are being held. Elections are the means to give practical form to the democratic principle of governance by the people, for the people, and of the people. Through elections, the people choose their representatives as their proxies, and from among these elected representatives, the government is formed, necessary policies, procedures, and laws are drafted for the state, the annual budget is prepared, and development construction plans are made. Therefore, as this election directly connects the people to the state, it also strengthens the democratic system. The election process, which began approximately 24 years ago in Athens, Greece, in Europe, has been brought into practice worldwide in a modern way since the 18th century, including in Australia, Britain, and America. It is known to all. In our country, Nepal, the electoral system seems to have started with the 2015 BS parliamentary elections. Honorable Chairperson, the upcoming election for the House of Representatives members is not a periodic election held regularly every 5 years as per our constitutional and legal provisions. This election is directly related to the Janjagruti movement of Bhadra 23rd and 24th. My own niece, Punam Gurung Thapamagar, who lives in Nepalgunj Dhamboji, and the son of Sushil Thapa Magar, Ayush Thapamagar, died in that movement. I wish to remember Ayush Thapamagar, my grandson, and all the adolescents and youths who died in the Janjagruti movement, and I wish for the speedy recovery of all those injured. I also express my sorrow over the vandalism and attacks on political parties and leaders that hijacked the Janjagruti movement, considering it extremely wrong. I wish to express my sorrow over this.
Honorable Chairperson, everyone knows how the Janjagruti movement of Bhadra 23rd and 24th started, where the Janjagruti movement began, what the demands and issues of the Janjagruti movement were, and how the movement, which later advanced with the demand to lift the ban on social media, led to the ousting of the government, the dissolution of the House of Representatives, and the formation of a non-party government. Although our opinions on this matter may differ, whatever happened, the country has gradually entered the election process. Nominations have been filed for the 164 direct and 110 proportional seats of the House of Representatives, and parties have also submitted their closed lists for proportional representation. The nomination of 3,084 candidates for direct elections, with only 395 women candidates, raises the question of what our understanding of women is, what the understanding of party leaders is. It is regrettable that all our parties, which advocate for equal rights, have failed to field even 10 percent women candidates. This needs to be corrected. I wish to draw the attention of all concerned parties through the Chairperson to make a legal provision to nominate at least 33 percent women as direct candidates.
Honorable Chairperson, the election day is approaching, but it is heard that the atmosphere is not yet as it should be for an election. It is also heard that questions are being raised about whether the elections will be free, fair, and free from fraud. If the elections cannot be held in a peaceful environment, and if some parties refuse to participate in a fearful environment, it is a matter of concern where the country will go. Everyone desires that this does not happen, and that all voters can participate in a fear-free election and exercise their right to vote freely. I hope that our constitutional system, which has reached the ICU, will recover and resume its work. I hope and expect that the government can honestly manage the special political situation and conduct the election successfully in the interest of the nation and the people. I expect that the candidates competing in the election arena will be able to fully uphold the democratic republic. It is also observed that some political parties have expressed disagreement with this system and are boycotting the elections, organizing various protest programs. I request all those parties to convey their views to the public without creating an atmosphere of fear and terror among the people.
Honorable Chairperson, our country Nepal is increasingly falling prey to geopolitical competition and conflict at the global level, and this is widely being discussed. There are also rumors of Nepal being divided in the eastern part. They say that the wind does not blow without reason; let this proverb not come true. Let no obstacle arise to our national unity. I repeat, let the elections be completed peacefully. Let our democratic system return to its rhythm, and let the state move forward on the path of development and prosperity with good governance. Honorable Chairperson, as far as I know, the movement of Bhadra 23rd was a movement of the youth with anger against corruption and for good governance in the country. The youth who came to the streets saying that doing good for the country is right and corruption is a crime were shot indiscriminately, innocent youths were killed. Remembering that incident still keeps me awake at night. How much pain must the parents of the youths who lost their lives in such a horrific incident be feeling? Only they would know. How much pain one feels when losing a loved one is only known to the person experiencing it, just as the edge of a khukuri is known only to the chopping block. Movements happen in the country and end; those who gain benefit, benefit, but those who lose cry remembering it for their entire lives. After all, who remembers the families of those who lost their children today? The movement of Bhadra 23rd was against corruption, but what was the movement of Bhadra 24th for? After all, some opportunists in the name of youth did not just burn leaders' houses, but also martyred innocent youths, destroyed public property, turned it to ashes, looted homes not just Big Mart and Bhatbhateni, but also private homes, overthrew the government, formed a new government, went to elections, and profited from it. What did the parents and families who lost their children get? Those who lost, lost, but their families cannot get their children back with money. Heartfelt tribute to those innocent youths who sacrificed their lives for the country. Heartfelt condolences to the parents and all the families of the children who lost their lives.
Honorable Chairperson, due to the failure to implement the budget for the fiscal year 2082/083 on time, many projects have been left incomplete. Whether the budget is small or large, a small budget may not make much difference in cities and towns, but even a small project can do a big job in remote districts. In our Karnali Province, there are still immense problems with roads, health, education, drinking water, and electricity. Honorable Chairperson, when development projects for the people are stopped, is that justice? We do not have an answer when asked why our development projects are stopped. Everyone talks about the suffering of the people due to movements, lack of development, and inadequate access to education and health facilities, but how can development happen if everyone forgets after coming to power? The current government has stopped the budgets allocated for projects, and the problems are only increasing. Therefore, I wish to draw the attention of the government through the Chairperson to the implementation of the stalled projects. Finally, I express my appreciation and thanks to the honorable members who completed their six-year term and are retiring on Falgun 20th, acknowledging their good work in the parliamentary committees. I also wish them continued success in their personal lives. Thank you. Jai Nepal.
Honorable Chairperson:- Honorable member Sumitra BC, time 10 minutes. After this,
(13:04 PM)
Honorable member Dr. Anjan Shakya.
Honorable Mr. Sumitra BC (Nepal Communist Party, UML):- And
(13:06 PM)
Honorable Chairperson Sir, I offer my heartfelt condolences to those who died in the jeep accident in Tripurasundari Municipality, Dolpa district on Magh 29th, and in the auto accident in Sitanagar Dad, Deukhuri, and wish for the speedy recovery of the injured. And Chairperson Sir, our Karnali Province is rich in various resources, but the people living there have to suffer constantly. The development agreement for the Upper Karnali Hydropower Project was made between the Government of Nepal and the Indian company GMR Upper Karnali Hydropower Limited. This project has been in a state of uncertainty for a long time due to the inability to secure financial management and start construction work. Although the agreement has been signed, its deadline has been extended multiple times, and the work has not progressed, while the deadline keeps getting extended. The agreement between the Investment Board and GMR was signed on Ashoj 3, 2071 BS. In this 900 MW project, a legal provision should be made to allow the local people to invest shares, and the project has not been able to move forward due to the lack of financial management. If the people also invest shares, I believe it will be financially viable and create a situation where the people feel a sense of ownership. Therefore, I wish for the attention of the upcoming government towards this. Despite repeated extensions, construction work has not practically begun on advancing this project within the deadline. I demand that the upcoming government pay timely attention. Also, Karnali Province has important medicinal herbs. To manage these herbs and to create awareness among the local people for income generation, to open small industries, to register companies, and to utilize the herbs of that region to advance the economic earnings of the local people, I request that the federal government be vigilant.
In the Bhairavi Rural Municipality of Dailekh, in the Jaljale area, drilling of 4000 meters is required to explore petroleum products in large quantities. Currently, 79 percent of the work has been completed, but it is now stalled at this point. The work of extracting petrol and methane gas, which can supply Nepal for 50 years, should be completed on time by the upcoming government, thereby making the economic future of the people of Nepal and Karnali Province bright.

I demand and believe that the upcoming government will get to work. Similarly, the earthquake victims of Jajarkot, who were hit by an earthquake on Kartik 17, 2080, are still unable to receive the funds to build their houses. The implementation process has been delayed, and there is a lack of budget, which is why it is said that a house can be completed with four lakh rupees. However, in today's inflation, it is impossible to build a house with that four lakh rupees. I request that this process be revised again so that the people of that region, who suffer from the cold in winter and from water in summer and rain, are not subjected to this problem. I want to demand that this problem be considered a national problem, as this natural problem can occur anytime, anywhere, and the people of those remote areas should receive facilities similar to other citizens of Nepal. Also, a bridge connecting Jajarkot and Rukum Paschim has been discussed many times in this assembly, and the people of that region have faced a lot of hardship due to the delay in the construction of this bridge. The contract for that bridge has now been canceled, and reports are coming in that no one wants to take the contract again. The reason for this is that the place where the bridge is being built is technically somewhat impossible to build. Therefore, by relocating the site, or by increasing the budget, or by whatever means necessary, if this bridge is built on time, the people of that region will benefit. I strongly demand that the government that will be formed after the elections of February 21 should pay timely attention to the problems of the Karnali region. I am a little concerned because, according to the report submitted by the Chief of the Commission for Investigation of Abuse of Authority, Nepal has ranked first in corruption. This is a matter of concern for all of us. The reason for being on the corruption list is that representatives from all three tiers of government – federal, provincial, and local – are involved, and goods worth 1 crore have been valued at up to 24 crores. It is reported that the money obtained through such corruption has gone to countries like America. I demand that strict action be taken against anyone, regardless of their party, person, or royal family, who engages in such corruption. I have heard news that the vehicle used by Balen Shah, who claims to provide good governance, was brought by businessman Kamal Kishore Malpani, who imported 14 vehicles by evading tax. We hear in the news that revenue of 2 crore 21 lakh 60 thousand 204 rupees was evaded while importing 14 vehicles. On one hand, tax is evaded, corruption is committed, and then it is claimed that there is no development in Nepal. If those who make such claims are not legally punished, and instead are glorified, perhaps we, the public, are also similar, which is why Nepal's development has not happened on time. I conclude my remarks by requesting that we be aware of this. Thank you. (13:06 PM) Presiding Officer: Honorable Vice Chairperson Ms. Vimla Ghimire. Honorable Chairperson: I (13:56 PM) Honorable Member Dr. Anjan Shakya. Time 5 minutes. After that, Honorable Member Renu Chand. 96 Honorable Dr. Anjan Shakya (Nominated): Honorable Chairperson, today, on the occasion of the conclusion of the 19th session of this glorious and respected National Assembly, I seek permission to present some of my thoughts and national concerns in the Provincial Concerns Hour. First of all, I pay my heartfelt tribute to the late Baldev Bohara, a senior politician and a dedicated and struggling leader of the Nepali Congress. His demise is not only a loss for Sudurpashchim but for the entire country. The presented report relates to the legislative interrelationships between federal units and relevant bodies. The Constitution of Nepal, from Schedule 4 to Schedule 9, outlines the exclusive and shared rights of the federal, provincial, and local levels. Based on this distribution of rights, all three levels can enact laws within their respective domains. In matters of shared rights, provincial assemblies, village assemblies, and municipal assemblies must enact laws that do not conflict with federal laws, and village assemblies and municipal assemblies must enact laws that do not conflict with provincial laws. The constitutional provision states that if there is a conflict, it will be invalid to the extent of the conflict. To understand the current state and problems of the law-making process in provincial assemblies and local levels, and to discuss the main achievements, challenges, and problems encountered in law-making, the responsible bodies and factors involved, and the future direction, as well as to exchange practices and experiences in the federal law-making process, interaction programs were organized with the provincial assembly committees and local levels of Sudurpashchim Province and Bagmati Province. Upon analyzing the facts obtained from the study and interactions, it is observed that although legislative practice has expanded at all three levels, the inter-level legislative interrelationship has not been as strong as expected. At the federal, provincial, and local levels, laws, rules, regulations, directives, procedures, standards, etc., have been formulated, leading to institutional development in legislative practice. However, the quality of the legislative process, consultation with stakeholders, and legislative review practices are weak, and the practical implementation of laws has not been ensured. Even after a decade of implementing the Constitution of Nepal, which adopted federalism, due to the lack of clear guidance, materials, and federal basic laws on matters of shared rights, there is confusion, duplicate law-making, and encroachment of rights at the provincial and local levels. Implementation and institutional weaknesses, including the current state of availability of legal personnel, make the creation of quality legislation extremely challenging. Honorable Chairperson, based on the conclusions drawn from interactions with local levels and provincial assembly committees, multifaceted reforms are necessary for quality legislative practice and strong inter-level legislative coordination. For this, it is necessary to ensure uniformity in the drafting of laws at the local and provincial levels and to prioritize law-making by mandating their use. The practice of measuring law implementation and reviewing jurisdiction should be institutionalized as an integral part of the legislative process. Furthermore, for the effective implementation of the Federal, Provincial, and Local Coordination and Interrelationship Act, 2077, the Legislation Act, 2081, and the laws enacted by provinces regarding the law-making of village and municipal assemblies, the capacity of local levels needs to be enhanced through their timely revision. In terms of human resources and institutional capacity, the need for skilled legal experts at the local level, and regular training on legislative practice, law drafting, and policy analysis for elected representatives and employees at the local and provincial levels is indispensable. To strengthen inter-level legislative coordination, a permanent coordination mechanism should be established between the federal, provincial, and local levels, a clear procedure should be developed to use federal laws as guidance for matters of shared rights, and existing law-making mechanisms and coordination meetings should be made policy-oriented, regular, and results-oriented. Additionally, an integrated digital legal database encompassing laws from all three levels needs to be created to enhance mutual compatibility and transparency. After the interim government was formed on 2082.5.27 BS, all proposals submitted to the Council of Ministers of the Government of Nepal on 2082.5.30 BS were withdrawn, and the said Immigration Bill was also withdrawn.
(b) The draft bill regarding immigration includes the issues identified by the esteemed Public Policy and Delegated Legislation Committee for amendment and policy reform in the Immigration Act. These include the entry, presence, visa issuance, visa types, visa fees, investigation, entry into controlled areas, obligations to be fulfilled by foreign citizens, monitoring and supervision of foreign citizens, and the power to deport and prohibit foreign citizens.

These include immigration-related matters. Similarly, the draft has been formulated by considering the country's needs and developed international practices regarding immigration. In the coming days, to further enrich the said legislative draft, all suggestions received after making it public for everyone in accordance with the provisions of the Legislative Act, 2081, will be incorporated. Likewise, the suggestions highlighted in the report of the esteemed committee will also be incorporated.
(c) Matters of delegated legislation under the Ministry of Home Affairs are being sent to the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs for registration in accordance with the provisions of the Legislative Act, 2081.
(d) By making the second amendment to the Immigration Procedures, 2065 on 2082.7.13, arrangements have been made for Nepali citizens to travel abroad on tourist visas based on their self-declaration of passport, visa, one-way destination ticket, and travel.
This has also improved past shortcomings.
49
(e) Regarding digital visas, a high-level study and investigation committee was formed by the Council of Ministers of the Government of Nepal on 2082.3.9. Regarding visit visas, the Ministry of Home Affairs has advanced the following reform measures.
(f) Regular work is being done to manage and digitize the visa system, and the immigration information system has been further strengthened. On 2082.8.11, a system for foreign national management information was arranged. Accordingly, the FOREIGN NATIONAL MANAGEMENT INFORMATIONS SYSTEM (FNMIS) has been brought into operation.
(g) In accordance with the provisions of the Legislative Act, 2081, the process of uploading and registering all delegated legislation on the website has been expedited.
(h) To make the service delivery provided by immigration user-friendly, regular training and refresher programs have been conducted for employees.
(i) The process of upgrading the Nepali Portal and further strengthening the immigration system has been expedited. An information system has been developed for the record and monitoring of the stay of foreign nationals in Nepal. International Card Payment has been initiated to facilitate visa acquisition and payment for foreign nationals. The system has been made fully online.
Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) is being made available online for foreign nationals visiting Nepal, and arrangements have been made for online payment of its fees.
Finally, I have taken the issues raised by the honorable members in the assembly through the honorable chairperson and the suggestions received seriously. I extend my heartfelt respect to the honorable members for this. Therefore, I respectfully request that the esteemed assembly and the proposed immigration bill by the Government of Nepal incorporate these suggestions received from the committee, which will be invaluable assets. The work related to immigration reform will be made effective. Thank you.

Honorable members, based on the issues raised by the honorable members in the discussion regarding the report and the views expressed by the honorable minister in response, the Government of Nepal is directed to implement the suggestions included in the study report regarding the Immigration Act, 2049 and the delegated legislation made thereunder, 2082, on a priority basis.
Honorable members, names have been received from the parties representing the National Assembly to present their views on the occasion of the conclusion of the ongoing session of the National Assembly. Now I will provide them with time sequentially. First, honorable member Dr. Beduram Bhusal.
Honorable Dr. Beduram Bhusal (Nepal Communist Party, Unified Socialist):-
(14:04 hrs)
Honorable Chairperson, the 19th session of our assembly began on January 18 and is concluding on February 12. We are concluding this session on the 27th day. During this period, we have held a total of eight meetings. On the first day, January 18, we concluded by expressing sorrow and passing a condolence motion on the demise of our honorable member Baldev Bohora. In the remaining seven meetings, we conducted the assembly's business based on the agenda. Looking at the work done in the seven meetings, we have passed three bills. We have accepted three ordinances. We had sent one bill to the committee for clause-by-clause discussion. The discussion there was almost complete. However, due to the government's incorrect stance on the subject matter of that bill, we could not pass it. We withdrew one bill at the government's request. Four study reports were presented during this period, including today, and we have discussed three of those reports. We could not discuss one report because today is the concluding day, and time is insufficient. The discussion on the study report regarding the legislative interrelationship between federal units, prepared by the Legislative Management Committee, was worth discussing. Similarly, it would have been even better if we had been able to discuss the report on the post-legislative scrutiny related to the Children Act. We could not do those things. However, the report on legislative interrelationship and the report on post-legislative scrutiny of the Children's Rights Act were presented here. We also held a question-and-answer session twice. Thus, looking back, I feel that doing so much work in such a short time in seven meetings is quite remarkable. I believe the success of this session lies in this. We may have to study whether we have done so much work in such a short time in the past; we have done it in this session, so I view it positively.
Honorable Chairperson, we are heading towards elections. The end of our session is due to going to elections. However, the question of what kind of environment these elections are being held in is arising. Will these elections be peaceful or not? Will they be impartial or not? Will they be free from fraud or not? And the question of whether the public, citizens, and voters will be able to cast their votes in a completely fear-free environment is seriously arising. I want to draw the government's serious attention to work harder to resolve this issue. It should play a more effective role, and the elections should be completed in such a way that the message goes out that the people's representatives have been elected and chosen in a truly peaceful, fair, fraud-free, and fear-free environment. I also demand that the government pay attention to this.
Similarly, in conclusion, I would like to request, Honorable Chairperson, this is the last meeting of this term for me, and this is my last speech. In this context, I would like to reiterate that what I say might be repetitive when expressing my experience: the standard that this assembly has set, the status it has achieved. If viewed from the perspective of the unique character of Nepali politics, it is somewhat above political disputes. Although we are members of political parties here, we cannot be completely free from disputes, nor can we be. However, in the context of the assembly's proceedings, and especially in the discussion and passing of bills, the consensus with which this assembly has worked, and similarly, the tradition of making decisions with consensus as much as possible on other matters, and making decisions by consensus, the traditions of starting work on time and completing tasks within the schedule, and the standards set by this assembly and its committees in the context of lawmaking. I hope this assembly can work in the coming days to raise all of them to a higher level. Even though we have many political differences, we can convey the message through this assembly that we can move forward with cooperation and consensus. With these few words of good wishes, I end my speech, which is not just a conclusion but also a farewell from this assembly. Perhaps we will meet again until the 20th, but in terms of expressing myself in this assembly, I would like to end my remarks in farewell to you all. Thank you.
Honorable Chairperson: - Honorable member Krishna Bahadur Rokaya.
(15:11 hrs)
Honorable Mr. Krishna Bahadur Rokaya (Nepali Congress):- Honorable Chairperson
(15:11 hrs)
Sir, the 19th session of the Federal Parliament, National Assembly, concludes today. This session began in January 2082 amidst a very politically volatile situation and uncertainty. First, I would like to offer my condolences on the sad demise of Honorable Baldev Bohora of the National Assembly and extend my heartfelt sympathy to his family. Indeed, Honorable Baldev Bohora made a significant contribution to Nepal's democratic movement, and I pay high respect to his contribution.
Similarly, this session was very short, and including today's meeting, we are concluding nine meetings today. I feel that this session has been very successful in this short period. Firstly, the question of whether the constitution is alive in this country or not, or the dignity and importance of the National Assembly, which many people had different understandings about. Therefore, this session has given the message that the constitution is still alive in this country. And similarly, I also feel that the dignity and importance of the National Assembly have been further enhanced.
Similarly, the nine meetings we held have resulted in very important decisions. We had five bills in the Legislative Committee, and out of those five bills, we have passed three bills with great effort and discussion. One bill has been withdrawn by the government itself, and we have given permission for that withdrawal from the committee and the assembly. While discussing one bill, some aspects were still lacking, and there were extensive discussions among the honorable members of the committee and the ministries. In this process, this bill required much more discussion. Therefore, due to lack of time, this one bill is still under consideration, and I believe this bill will be passed in the next session. Similarly, during this period, the chairpersons of many committees and the committees worked very hard and presented their reports to the assembly. Those reports have been passed, and I urge the government to implement those reports in the future, and in some cases, to enact legislation. And specifically regarding the committees, I am in the Legislative Committee. The chairperson of my committee, Honorable Tulsi Dahal, worked very hard. Indeed, all the...

We have passed and sent many bills from this assembly during his tenure. Many bills have also been zeroed out when sent to the House of Representatives. But as of today, he has worked very hard. I want to praise him for this hard work, his contribution to this committee, and his contribution to this assembly. I want to honor him and congratulate him. 

Following this, along with the bills, the Government of Nepal has also brought three ordinances in the interim, including an ordinance to amend some voter laws. The government had brought the Names Act, 2073. And we have also worked to pass those ordinances from here. Therefore, I would like to request again, and I want to reiterate, that this session has been extremely successful in this short period, I would like to inform the honorable house again. 

After this, some honorable members who have completed their six-year term are going to retire, and I want to express my heartfelt congratulations to all the honorable members who are retiring, that there has been immense cooperation with them during my two-year tenure. And they have worked very hard. Their qualifications, their capabilities, and their contributions to the National Assembly are highly commendable and will serve as a guide for the National Assembly and for me. Therefore, I wish all the honorable members who are retiring a more successful and pleasant future in their political careers. 

Similarly, elections are going to be held in this country on Falgun 21, 2082 BS. This election is not a regular election like the past, nor is it a periodic election. In an unusual circumstance in the country, due to the incident of Bhadra 23 and 24, and today, none of us can actually accept that the dissolution of the House of Representatives is legal. However, the country is holding elections in a different time and circumstance. Therefore, everyone is concerned and worried about this election. Honorable members have also mentioned this earlier, that today, common citizens are still wondering whether the election will be held on Falgun 21? Whether that election will be fair, free from fraud, and peaceful? And whether the outcome of that election, after it is completed, will provide a way out for the current political situation of the country? This is a major question today, a serious question. Therefore, I urge the government to make this election peaceful, fair, and free from fraud, and may the outcome of this election truly provide a way out for the country. However, I want to mention one thing: it is said that this is a government formed according to the aspirations of the youth. It is a government of the citizens, a government of independent citizens. And I think some ministers define themselves that way. But today, some members of the government are rushing to contest the election. Some members, by not fulfilling their responsibilities, their duties, their obligations, are themselves going to contest the election, and some remaining members are conducting the election today. Therefore, is this a coincidence or what? I wish it is just a coincidence. I wish only this. And if there are indeed other things, people have many expectations. If there are some things beyond that position, those things will be revealed in the future. Therefore, I urge again through this honorable chairperson to this honorable house, this honorable assembly, that the election to be held on Falgun 21 be extremely fair, peaceful, and free from fraud. Let an environment be created where common Nepali citizens, voters, can vote for the party and candidate of their choice in an environment free from fear, and may the subsequent outcome truly provide a way out for this country. May that way out strengthen the nation. May that way out strengthen the democratic system, and may that way out ensure that no one can tamper with the constitution. May the constitution be strengthened. And for this, I urge all political parties, who have contributed to the creation of this constitution and the establishment of this federal democratic republic, to unite and create an environment after the 21st, and let us all unite for the prosperity and development of this country. I conclude my remarks here. Thank you. Jai Nepal. 

Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Gopal Bhattarai. 
(15:22 hrs) 
Honorable Mr. Gopal Bhattarai (Nepal Communist Party, UML): Honorable Chairperson, today we are at the end of the 19th session, and I am at the end of my presence in this assembly rather than individually. Therefore, I extend my heartfelt thanks to everyone. Since I entered this assembly, I have had the opportunity to work in various committees and the opportunity to cooperate with various honorable members. Therefore, I believe that the cooperation with you all has been a learning experience for me. Honorable Chairperson, even in this adverse situation, not only in this adverse situation but also in a situation of uncertainty, we have been able to conduct this assembly. The assembly that was burnt down and destroyed, and there was no place to hold its meetings, the chairperson and the secretariat worked to arrange for a place and get the government to agree, and with our support and cooperation, this assembly resumed, as honorable members have said. This assembly's final meeting, the final session, has accomplished many tasks. We have held 9 meetings, including today. We passed a condolence motion in one of them. Apart from that, every meeting has done important work, and a lot of work has been done. Passing 3-4 bills in 9 meetings within a month is not a small feat. We also worked very hard in the committee, and we have received the fruits of that labor. I wish that the honorable members who will be here in the future and the new honorable members will continue this cooperation. I would say to leave the aggressiveness towards some people, some leaders, that is still remaining. Repeatedly raising one issue, saying that so-and-so did this, or if it had been done differently, if the work done by them was wrong and not in accordance with the rules, then what have those who have been in government repeatedly been looking at? It needs to be resolved. If it is not resolved, coming to the assembly and speaking for public consumption, I urge that this should not be done. Now, regarding the work we have done so far, as much as we could do. After we entered, Corona weakened us for two years. After that, various incidents occurred, but I believe we have done a lot of work through hard work. Now, there are some things that need to be done immediately. Laws that need to be enacted for the implementation of federalism, which the Legislation Committee has indicated to the government, need to be brought quickly. We need to create pressure on the government to bring those laws quickly, and because those laws are not being made, it seems like federalism might fail. Therefore, to make it successful, these laws are very necessary, I believe. Now, regarding this matter, I have only stated these things, and before this, I have already thanked all the honorable members. Therefore, I will not go into this further. 

Now, what is being seen is that elections are coming. If the elections are fair, independent, and free from fraud, there is no doubt. But why is there doubt? Because issues of corruption are being withdrawn, and the government is withdrawing them. It is a separate matter that the court is not accepting them, but the government is involved in it. If others are called corrupt, the government's attitude of withdrawing issues like corruption and organized crime also casts doubt on whether this election will be fair and free from fraud. Those people escaped from jail, brought out many people, completed their tasks, and then went back to jail. Then all the burning also happened afterwards. Therefore, we have no basis to trust this. The state of peace and security is not good. People are scared. It is not as easy here as we see. The police administration today is seen to be staying close, fearing the people who went to welcome the king there. Therefore, when the morale of the police administration is falling, how can the morale of the public rise? We do not see any signs that this will be fair and free from fraud based on these matters. Now, weapons looted by the police are outside. Visuals with photos of those who burned down Singha Durbar, burned down the court, burned down the parliament, have come out. None of those people have been caught. Some have become candidates. After that, how will there be peace and security? And we have no basis to believe that these elections will be fair. The state of social media is also like that. The Election Commission has said that it cannot control social media. If the police administration says, 'Do what you can,' then how will it happen? Based on these matters, we have no basis to believe that the elections will be held with peace and security. Now, as I said before, it was not possible to finish in 1 minute. Just now, 16 employees have been dismissed from the Social Welfare Council. Does the code of conduct apply to the government or not? Are those actions being taken after the code of conduct has come into effect? That will be decided after the election is over. If the government they want comes, it will decide, or if another government comes, it will decide. Even in such matters, the government is getting involved, and the situation appears to be somewhat one-sided. Therefore, I have taken a little more time, and I apologize for this. In such a situation, with only 15-20 days left for the election, I want to draw the government's attention to how it can send a message that the election will be fair and free from fraud within these 20 days. Thank you. 

Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Tul Prasad Bishwakarma. 
(15:33 hrs) 
Honorable Mr. Tul Prasad Bishwakarma (Rastriya Janamorcha): Honorable Chairperson, Honorable Members, and other staff colleagues, today we are at the closing ceremony of the 19th session, and at this time, one-third of the honorable members are retiring. And our honorable Vice-Chairperson of the National Assembly is also among them. The cooperation we received during our time with them was extremely important. I want to thank them on behalf of all the honorable members for their discussions, work, guidance, and support. We have done a lot of work. As the previous speaker said, we have accomplished a lot in this session compared to other sessions. We must accept that we have done a lot in such a short period in terms of duration. 

And now we are going to the elections, the country is going to the elections. On the 21st, our voting...

The country is in a state of great uncertainty and anxiety. There is an atmosphere of uncertainty and concern. There is doubt as to whether elections will be held in a fear-free environment. However, we are compelled to go to elections. Therefore, I request the government to be fully committed to ensuring impartial elections and creating an environment where the public can express their opinions without fear. I wish to make this request. Amidst this election environment, news has also appeared in the press about various places where weapons have been found and money has been seized. Weapons confiscated by the police are now out. Many escaped criminals are out of jail. Therefore, the situation is extremely serious. On the other hand, the country's political situation has reached an extremely serious point. Specifically, the nation's nationality, sovereignty, and integrity are at stake. To be honest, the country's existence is in question, and such a situation has arisen. We are all assessing the situation. We are listening to what is reported in the press and media. We are observing the activities within the country. Does this negate the nation's nationality? Such a question has arisen starkly, and we are seeing it in the press. Recently, the chief of the Indo-Pacific Strategy visited and met directly with the Nepali Army, according to the press. Following this, a writer in a Chinese newspaper wrote that you are doing one thing and saying another. It said, either follow your history and live safely, or face the consequences of your actions. Such statements are being made. We are going to elections in such a situation. This is the country's condition today. On one hand, this is the situation, and on the other hand, as we have been saying for a long time, this federalism has become a burden on the country. This federalism has added ethnic and regional discord and economic burden to the country, so let's consider it. Our efforts are still focused on strengthening and consolidating it. We have tried for a long time, but we have not achieved significant results. Now, we ourselves are questioning whether the country will survive with federalism. In that situation, we are back to square one. We have all seen the machinations of domestic and foreign power centers, and to what extent they have reached. Therefore, I wish to state my view here that this matter also needs consideration. Populist politics has become extremely dominant in other countries. For a long time, the Rana regime ended, the Panchayat system was overthrown, monarchy was abolished, and in its place, a republic was established. Secularism was introduced. In this movement, leaders and political parties who sacrificed their lives have no recognition. Those who emerged overnight, who sprouted overnight, are standing in the electoral field based on stunts. Among them, many are directly involved in the arson and chaos that occurred during the Madhes movement. We are seeing their candidacies in the elections. Not only that, but the issue of re-establishing Hinduism and bringing back the monarchy is being raised loudly today. Why has this issue arisen? Those of us who held power in the past, we major parties that were in power, have definitely not been able to move the country in the right direction. We have not been able to deliver properly to the people. We have not been able to address the people's voices. This is why such an environment has been created, and we see it in the press regarding those running in the elections. Some ten pastors are candidates here. On one hand, there is a rush to Christianize this country, and on the other hand, there is a rush to make it a Hindu state. What will happen to the country in the midst of this tug-of-war? Where will it go? This is a situation that we all need to take seriously and think about. Similarly, we have repeatedly raised the issue of MCC in the house. MCC is detrimental to the country. This MCC project has not come with a purely charitable intention. It has a strategic reason behind it, and that is that it is a part of the Indo-Pacific Strategy. Today, its true nature is gradually being revealed. Gradually, its representatives are coming and meeting. And frankly, the major parties that were in power repeatedly in the past took the MCC to parliament and passed it. That same MCC has overthrown them. It has brought this government down and brought the country to this point. Therefore, we could not discern such things in time, we could not understand them in time, and we could not take any steps. Today, the issue of abolishing the constitution is being raised. The abolition of the constitution is definitely aimed at abolishing the republic, secularism, and the multi-party system, and in its place, bringing back the monarchy and making it a Hindu state. Therefore, we must be serious about this issue and oppose the abolition of the constitution. We must all be firm and united in amending the minor flaws in the constitution and continuing this system forward. I wish to state this here. Furthermore, the issue of an executive head is also being raised here, and specifically, many leftist parties have also said there should be an executive head. However, in the context of Nepal, it may be suitable for some countries, but in the context of Nepal, we believe that an executive head is not suitable. Because in the current prime ministerial system, there is a check and balance. But in a small country like ours, with such political chaos, if there is an executive head, arbitrariness can arise. If that executive head is not accountable to the people and becomes arbitrary, what will be the fate of the country? If a single executive head is allowed, just as Sikkim merged with India, it will not take long for Nepal to merge. There is no doubt about that. Therefore, I think we need to be aware of this issue. Therefore, whatever happens in the coming days, the country has now entered the election process. And this government should conduct this election impartially with utmost caution and care, manage the security mechanisms, and create an environment for the public to cast their votes without fear. And the government that comes next should play a role in protecting the nation's nationality, sovereignty, the multi-party system brought by the people's struggle, fundamental rights, and other important things, and move the country forward, making it a self-reliant and self-respecting nation. I wish to conclude my remarks by expressing this hope. I also apologize for taking up too much time. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable members, the 18th session ended amidst uncertainty and anxiety. Now, as the 19th session is concluding, the situation has changed significantly. We have now reached the threshold of the House of Representatives elections. An election atmosphere has been created across the country. When the 19th session began on Magh 4th, we had new challenges and new responsibilities on our shoulders. We have fulfilled them skillfully. I would also like to recall here that compared to previous sessions of the National Assembly, this session has been very short in terms of time and very important in terms of work, and it would be no exaggeration to say that we can be proud of it in the future. From managing the new hall required for the session to managing all the technology, despite everything being new, due to the active cooperation of all honorable members and the active initiative of the Federal Parliament Secretariat and all its subordinate bodies, we have reached the end of the 19th session without any hindrance or obstruction. Honorable members, the first meeting of the twenty-ninth session of the Federal Parliament, National Assembly, commenced on Sunday, Magh 4, 2082, at 11:00 AM and continued until Friday, Falgun 1, 2082, for a total of 27 days. During this period, 9 meetings were held, and a total of 17 hours and 24 minutes were spent on the work of the assembly. During this session, there was a zero hour in 7 meetings. In the said zero hour, 29 honorable members utilized 48 minutes, while there was a special time in 3 meetings. In the special time, 15 honorable members utilized 3 hours and 39 minutes. One meeting of this session had a provincial concern time. In the provincial concern time, 7 honorable members utilized 1 hour and 18 minutes. In order to present their experiences gained while serving in the assembly and committees, 11 honorable members utilized 2 hours and 12 minutes during the period when honorable members retiring on Falgun 20, 2082, presented their experiences. Honorable members, the Bill on Intangible Cultural Heritage (Conservation), 2081, registered in the assembly, has been sent to the Legislation Management Committee for clause-wise discussion, while the Tourism Bill, 2081, the Film Bill, 2081, and the National Forensic Science Laboratory (Establishment and Operation) Bill, 2081, have been passed and sent to the House of Representatives, and the Government of Nepal has withdrawn the Social Media Bill, 2081. Honorable members, during this period, the Ordinance to Amend the Voter Roll Act, 2073, 2082; the Ordinance to Amend the House of Representatives Election (First Amendment), 2082; and the Nepal Special Service Act (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 2082, have been presented in the assembly and unanimously approved. As an important tool for making the government accountable to the parliament, 4 oral question-and-answer sessions related to the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, the Ministry of Federal Affairs and General Administration, and the Ministry of Finance were held during this session. Honorable members, at the beginning of the session, Honorable Member Narayan Kaji Shrestha and Honorable Member Bhagwati Neupane, elected from Gandaki Province in the 2076 National Assembly member election, and Honorable Member Bamdev Gautam, nominated by the Right Honorable President, resigned in writing in accordance with clause (a) of Article 89 of the Constitution of Nepal. Honorable Member Baldev Bohara, elected from Sudurpaschim Province in the 2080 National Assembly member election, passed away. The seats of the aforementioned National Assembly members have become vacant. As per the constitutional provision, as one-third of the honorable members complete their six-year term and retire, new members have been elected in the vacant posts on Magh 11 during the session. We will meet them in the 20th session. In this regard, we extend our heartfelt thanks and best wishes for a bright future to the retiring honorable members, and congratulations and best wishes for a successful term to the newly elected honorable members. Honorable members, during this session, Honorable Chairperson Kamala Pant of the Development, Economic Affairs and Good Governance Committee presented the Study Report on National Integrity Policy, 2082, and the Annual Report of the Development, Economic Affairs and Good Governance Committee for the fiscal year 2081/082; Honorable Chairperson Maya Prasad Sharma of the Public Policy and Delegated Legislation Committee presented the Study Report on the Immigration Act, 2049, and the delegated legislation made thereunder, 2082, and the Annual Report of the Public Policy and Delegated Legislation Committee for the fiscal year 2081/082; Honorable Chairperson Sonam Geljen Sherpa of the Federalism Strengthening and National Concern Committee presented...

The Committee on Empowerment and National Concern presented the annual report for the fiscal year 2081/82, and the Chairperson of the Legislation Management Committee, Honourable Tulsa Kumari Dahal, presented the annual report of the Legislation Management Committee for the fiscal year 2081/082, the report on legislative interrelationships among federal units: study report, 2082, and the report on measuring the implementation of provisions related to child participation in the Children Act, 2075, 2082. Furthermore, among the reports presented to the House, the study report on National Integrity Policy, 2082; the Immigration Act, 2049 report, 2082; and the study report on policy issues related to national parks, 2082, which was presented in the previous session and is pending discussion, were discussed in the House. The directives were also issued to implement the suggestions included in the report and the commitments expressed by the Right Honourable Prime Minister and Honourable Ministers from the government's side on a priority basis. During this session, the annual report of the Muslim Commission for the fiscal year 2080/081 has been presented to the House in accordance with the constitutional provision. Honourable members, during this session, the House passed a condolence motion on the demise of National Assembly member Baldev Bohara, former minister and former member of the House of Representatives Rishikesh Gautam, former minister, Constituent Assembly member and former member of the House of Representatives Mohammad Aftab Alam, former member of the National Assembly Krishnakumari Shrestha, former minister, former member of the House of Representatives and National Assembly member Amod Prasad Upadhyay, former minister and former member of the House of Representatives Homanath Dahal, and former member of the National Assembly Shukraraj Shastri. Honourable members, although the 19th session of the National Assembly was conducted for a short period in terms of time, it has been completed by fulfilling a historic and important role. In the changed political situation of the country after the Jana Andolan and in the context of the dissolution of the House of Representatives and the announcement of new elections, we have accomplished specific tasks through the National Assembly amidst a kind of uncertainty. The National Assembly has played a parental role by not only resolving legal complexities but also by building mutual trust in accordance with the spirit of the constitution through agreement, cooperation, and coordination with the government, federal parliament, political parties, and other stakeholders, and by dispelling the uncertainty that arose among the public. Finally, I express my special thanks and gratitude to the Right Honourable President, the Right Honourable Prime Minister, Honourable Ministers, National Assembly members, political parties, the Secretary-General of the Federal Parliament, the Secretary of the House, the Secretariat Secretary, all the staff, and all the security personnel who played an important role in successfully completing the 19th session. Thank you. Reporter - Honourable members, a letter has been received from the Right Honourable President regarding the conclusion of the ongoing twenty-ninth session. Now, I will inform you of the contents of the said letter. Honourable Speaker, National Assembly, Singhdarbar, Kathmandu. In accordance with Article 93, Sub-section (2) of the Constitution, upon the recommendation of the Council of Ministers of the Government of Nepal dated 2082/10/26, the ongoing session of the National Assembly has been concluded, effective from Friday, Falgun 1, 2082, at 12:00 AM midnight. (Ram Chandra Poudel) President 2082 Magh 29. Honourable members, I declare this meeting adjourned, with the ongoing twenty-ninth session of the National Assembly automatically concluding from tonight at 12:00 AM. Adjourned: 95:56.

sections.name: Opening
sections.summary_en: The speaker draws attention to the pollution of rivers in Kathmandu, urging the government to clean them. They also criticize the 'Asare' development (monsoon development) for causing public suffering and wasting budget. The speaker congratulates newly elected members of the National Assembly and bids farewell to departing members.

speakers.name: Honorable Member Ganga Kumari Belbase
speakers.topic: River pollution, monsoon development, congratulations to new members

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: Honorable Ganga Kumari Belbase discusses the potential of Bagmati Province, highlighting its geography, demographics, and resources. She emphasizes the need for industrial development, improved infrastructure, and tourism promotion. She also addresses challenges in agriculture, education, health, and hydropower, urging government action on issues like unmanaged settlements and contract cancellations.

speakers.name: Honorable Mr. Ganga Kumari Belbase
speakers.topic: Potential and challenges of Bagmati Province

sections.name: Adjournment
sections.summary_en: The Chairperson announces the conclusion of the provincial concerns session and informs the house about a letter regarding the assignment of ministerial responsibilities. The Minister of Agriculture and Livestock Development is going abroad, and his portfolio will be temporarily handled by Minister Anil Kumar Sinha.
